record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: Outside the trivial situations listed in the survey—such as convex coercive costs on a closed convex control set or convex costs on a closed bounded convex control set—can one prove the existence of optimal controls for stochastic distributed parameter systems, for example via a verification theorem or by proving compactness of minimizing sequences in genuinely nontrivial settings?

evidence.quote: (10) Existence of optimal controls. We have discussed the necessary conditions for optimal controls without proving the existence of an optimal control, which is a very difficult problem. There are two general approaches available to study it. One is to prove the verification theorem, the other is to show that a minimizing sequence of controls is compact. Both methods have not been developed well for SDPSs. Except for some trivial cases ... there is no further result for that problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geq 0},\mathbb{P})$ be a complete filtered probability space on which a cylindrical Wiener process $W(\cdot)$ is defined. Let $H$ and $U$ be separable Hilbert spaces, $A:\mathcal{D}(A)\subset H\to H$ the generator of a $C_0$-semigroup, and consider the controlled stochastic evolution equation
$$dy(t)=\bigl(Ay(t)+b(t,y(t),u(t))\bigr)\,dt+\sigma(t,y(t),u(t))\,dW(t),\quad t\in[0,T],\quad y(0)=y_0\in H,$$
where $u(\cdot)$ is an $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$-progressively measurable process taking values in a nonempty set $\mathcal{U}\subset U$, and $b,\sigma$ are measurable mappings of suitable regularity ensuring well-posedness in a class $\mathcal{Y}$ of mild solutions. Let the cost functional be
$$J(u(\cdot))=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^T f(t,y(t),u(t))\,dt+h(y(T))\right],$$
where $f$ and $h$ are measurable functions, possibly nonconvex in $u$ and not necessarily coercive, and where the control set $\mathcal{U}$ is not assumed to be both bounded and convex.

Prove or disprove: outside the trivial situations (in which $\mathcal{U}$ is closed and convex with $J$ convex and coercive in $u$, or in which $\mathcal{U}$ is closed bounded and convex with $J$ convex in $u$), there exists an admissible control $u^\ast(\cdot)$ minimizing $J$. Specifically, develop either
(i) a verification theorem identifying an optimal control through the value function or an associated Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman / Riccati-type equation, or
(ii) a compactness argument showing that any minimizing sequence $\{u_n(\cdot)\}$ admits a subsequence whose corresponding state-control pair converges to an admissible optimal pair,
in a genuinely nontrivial setting for the above class of stochastic distributed parameter systems.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature indicates that existence of optimal controls for stochastic distributed parameter systems (controlled SPDEs) is well understood only in special cases (e.g., convex coercive costs on closed convex control sets, or convex costs on closed bounded convex control sets). General verification theorems and compactness-of-minimizing-sequences techniques have not been developed beyond these trivial cases. Recent surveys on control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems list this as an open problem; we found no publication establishing a general existence result in genuinely nontrivial settings.

status_evidence.title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing recent progress and open problems on control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems, including existence of optimal controls.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of optimal controls for SDPSs is identified as an open problem outside trivial cases.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical Control Theory for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Treatise on stochastic PDE control: many tools for deterministic distributed-parameter and stochastic finite-dimensional systems do not extend to SDPSs.
status_evidence.claim: Standard methods for proving existence of optimal controls do not yet work in the SDPS setting.

status_evidence.title: Control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems, an engineering perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses interconnections between existence of optimal controls, solvability of the optimality system, and the associated Riccati equation.
status_evidence.claim: Existence remains tied to unresolved questions about optimality systems and Riccati equations for SDPSs.
